مُوَطَّأُ الأَكْنَافِ , (K,) and الاكناف ↓ وَطِىْءُ , (TA,) A man of easy nature, or disposition, generous, and very hospitable: or one in whose vicinity his companion is possessed of power, authority, or dignity; not harmed, nor inconveniently situated. (K.) ―
-b2- اللّٰهُمَّ ٱجْعَلْهُ مُوَطَّأَ العَقِبِ (assumed tropical:) O God, make him to be (a Sultán, followed by many dependants, and) one whose heels shall be trod upon: (K *, TA:) an imprecation, occurring in a trad. respecting a man who had been secretly informed against to 'Omar, who said this with reference to the informer if a liar. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
